# Helping Your Midwife Find You
### Riverside Community Midwives: Home Birth Welcome Pack

Hello! When labour starts, we want to get to you quickly and calmly, without driving round the block six times or knocking on the wrong door.

This page is full of small things that make a big difference. Some of them we learned the hard way, and there are a few true stories in here to prove it. Please have a read, share it with whoever will be at home with you, and stick the checklist at the end on your fridge.

---

## First things first: 37 weeks

**Our home birth cover starts from 37 weeks.**

Before 37 weeks, your birth is planned at the hospital. If labour starts early, please phone **[hospital maternity line / triage number]** and go to the hospital as normal.

We tell everyone this at the booking visit, but we know there is a lot to remember. Write it on the calendar so it doesn't get lost.

---

## When labour starts: who to call

**Phone the Riverside Birth Line: [number]**

- **Always use the Birth Line, not a midwife's personal mobile.** The Birth Line goes to whoever is on call that day or night. Your favourite midwife might be asleep, on holiday, or at another birth, so the Birth Line is the fastest way to get help.
- When you call, tell us:
  - your **name**
  - your **address**, including the flat number and building
  - **how many weeks** pregnant you are
  - **what is happening** (for example, contractions, waters breaking, bleeding)
  - **anything tricky** about finding you or getting in
- **Send your location** to the Birth Line phone. Either:
  - send a **location pin on WhatsApp**, or
  - send your **what3words** address (free app, gives every 3-metre square its own three words)

  Honestly, this is brilliant. Do it even if you think your house is easy to find.

**In an emergency, call 999.**

---

## Two midwives, two cars

For the birth, **two midwives** will come to you, usually in **separate cars**. One arrives first and the second joins later.

If you can, please **save two parking spaces** as close to your door as possible. Move your own car round the corner, ask a neighbour nicely, or put the wheelie bins out (then take them back in when we arrive!).

### Why does close parking matter so much?

We carry **a lot**: gas and air cylinders (Entonox), our big bag of equipment, and sometimes birthing pool bits as well. By the third trip from the car, our arms are tired. A short walk means we're with you faster.

---

## Permit parking (Anfield, Kensington and other zones)

If you live in a **permit parking zone**, including around **Anfield and Kensington**, please sort out a **visitor permit** from the council before 37 weeks. If you can, get **two**.

Keep them **by the front door** so we can grab one and put it on the dashboard. We have had parking tickets at births before. We don't want to find one on the windscreen at 5am after a lovely birth!

On match days, parking around Anfield can be very hard. If your due date is near the football season, have a plan.

---

## Make your house easy to find

### Your house number

Make sure your **house number is easy to see from the road**, on the door, the gate, or the wall.

> **True story:** One family lived at a house with no number, only a name: "Rosemary Cottage." It was in a street of terraced houses. The sat nav took me to the chippy. Smelled lovely, but no baby there.

If your house has a name and no number, **tell us when you call**, and give us a landmark ("three doors up from the corner shop, green door").

### Flats and big buildings

If you live in a flat, please tell us:
- the **building name or block letter** as well as the flat number
- which **entrance** to use
- the **buzzer** or door code
- whether there is a **lift**, and if it works

> **True story:** I once drove round a block of flats in Everton for 20 minutes. Flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in a different building! In the end, the dad was waving a tea towel out of the window. It worked, but a WhatsApp pin would have been quicker.

### Porch light on, please!

At night, especially in winter, **every dark street looks the same**. When you phone the Birth Line, **switch on your porch light or front room light**, and leave the curtains open a little so we can see which house is yours.

### Make it obvious

> **Best idea ever:** One family tied **balloons to their gate**, like a birthday party. I found them straight away. Nobody else on the street had balloons at 2am.

Balloons, a bright scarf on the gate, a sign in the window. Anything that says "it's this one!" is perfect.

### Open door? Be ready to meet us

If you can, have someone **watching for us** and ready to open the door.

> **True story:** Once, the front door was open, so I walked straight in. It was the wrong house. A very nice older gentleman gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway. Lovely man, but no baby.

---

## Inside the house

### Clear the way

Please clear the **path, hallway and stairs**: shoes, washing baskets, bags, toys and **especially Lego**. We will be carrying heavy things, sometimes in the dark, sometimes in a hurry. Nobody wants a midwife on crutches.

### Pets

We love animals, really we do. But during labour, and especially during the pushing, **please put pets in another room** with the door shut.

> **True story:** There was a Staffie called Pippin who loved me *too* much. Every visit he jumped all over me. One time I nearly dropped the Entonox cylinder. Pippin was a good boy, but he was much happier with a chew in the kitchen.

Ask someone to look after your pet if you can, or have a safe room ready.

### A little bit of space

It helps to have:
- a **clear space** near where you want to give birth
- **somewhere to put our equipment** (a corner of the floor is fine)
- **good light** we can switch on when we need it

You don't need to tidy the whole house. We are not here to look at your skirting boards!

---

## We are coming as a friend

In the Philippines, where one of our midwives grew up, people say **the midwife is like family**. That's how we want you to feel about us.

We're not coming to judge your house, your parking, or your dog. We're coming to look after you and your baby, in your own home, where you feel safe. Everything on this page just helps us get to you quickly so we can do that.

If you have any questions about home birth, or about anything on this page, ask us at any visit. No question is silly. We have heard them all, and we have probably been lost on your street at least once.

**See you soon!**
*From all of us at Riverside Community Midwives*

---

## ✂ Fridge Checklist: "Ready for the Midwife"

**Before 37 weeks:**

☐ I know home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**
☐ I know to phone **[hospital number]** if labour starts before 37 weeks
☐ **Riverside Birth Line** number saved in my phone and my partner's phone: **[number]**
☐ **what3words** app downloaded / I know how to send a **WhatsApp location pin**
☐ **Visitor parking permits** ready by the front door (if I'm in a permit zone)
☐ House number **easy to see** from the road
☐ Plan for **two parking spaces**
☐ Plan for **pets** (another room or someone to look after them)

**When labour starts:**

☐ Phone the **Birth Line**, not a midwife's own mobile
☐ Tell them: name, address, weeks pregnant, what is happening, how to find us
☐ Send our **location pin or what3words** to the Birth Line phone
☐ **Porch light on**, curtains open a little
☐ Balloons or something bright on the gate (optional but brilliant!)
☐ **Path, hallway and stairs clear**: no shoes, no washing, no Lego
☐ **Pets** in another room
☐ Someone ready to **watch for us and open the door**

**Emergency? Call 999.**

---

A few things for you to fill in or check before it goes out:

- **[number] placeholders.** I didn't want to guess the Birth Line and hospital numbers, so pop those in.
- **The 999 line.** I added "In an emergency, call 999." It wasn't in your notes but it seemed wise for a home birth handout. Worth a quick check with Deb that it matches what the team usually tells families.
- **The Philippines bit.** I wrote it as "one of our midwives." If you'd rather put your name on the page, it could become "In the Philippines, where I grew up…" and you could sign it from you.
